system_category.reference: In this paper, we explore a simple approach having the best of both worlds, by building on the exciting developments in generative modeling and retrieval for open domain question answering.

knowledge_representation.reference: This method proceeds in two steps, by first retrieving supporting passages using either sparse or dense representations. Then, a sequence-to-sequence model generates the answer, taking as input the retrieved passages in addition to the question.

retrieval_mechanism.reference: For the retrieval of support passages, we consider two methods: BM25 (Robertson et al., 1995) and DPR (Karpukhin et al., 2020).

knowledge_source.reference: In BM25, passages are represented as bag of words, and the ranking function is based on term and inverse document frequencies. We use the implementation from Apache Lucene with default parameters... In DPR, passages and questions are represented as dense vector representations... Retrieval is performed using approximate nearest neighbors with the FAISS library.
